questions.stem: What is the difference between a symptom and a cause in debugging?

options.text: A symptom is the underlying defect; a cause is the observable error.
A symptom is the observable error; a cause is the underlying defect.
Both are the same and interchangeable.
A symptom is an error in syntax; a cause is an error in logic.

questions.explanation: In debugging, a symptom is the error you observe, while the cause is the defect in the code that leads to this error. Addressing the cause is necessary to resolve the symptom.

questions.stem: If a program's logic error causes it to output 15 instead of the expected 10, what is the percentage error? Provide your answer as a percentage.
questions.explanation: The percentage error is calculated as ((15 - 10) / 10) * 100% = 50%. This measures the deviation of the observed value from the expected value.

questions.stem: Explain why it is important to distinguish between a symptom and a cause when debugging a program.
markingGuide: Understanding the symptom helps identify the observable error.
Identifying the cause allows you to address the root of the problem.
Fixing only the symptom may not resolve the underlying issue.
questions.explanation: Distinguishing between symptom and cause is crucial because fixing the symptom alone may not solve the underlying defect. Understanding the cause allows you to implement a solution that addresses the root of the problem, preventing future errors.
